In nineteen thirty-two, Australia went to war with birds. And lost.
About twenty thousand emus had invaded the wheat farms of Western Australia.
The farmers were ex-soldiers. So they asked the government for machine guns.
A major arrived with two soldiers, two Lewis guns, and ten thousand rounds of ammunition.
The emus split into small groups. Then a gun jammed.
In the first ambush, they got about twelve birds.
Within a week, the army was pulled out.
By December, they'd fired nearly ten thousand rounds.
The major claimed under a thousand kills. Historians think even that was generous.
His verdict? They can face machine guns with the invulnerability of tanks.
The army never went back. The emus are still there.
A trained army lost, because it underestimated what it was up against.
